name: XL Recordings
description: British independent record label founded in London in 1989 by Tim Palmer and Nick Halkes as an offshoot of Beggars Banquet's dance label Citybeat, to release rave and dance music. Run and co-owned by Richard Russell since 1996, it forms part of the Beggars Group, releases an average of six albums a year across genres, and counts Adele, Dizzee Rascal, M.I.A., Radiohead, Vampire Weekend, The xx, and Gil Scott-Heron among its roster. Early success came with the Prodigy's Music for the Jilted Generation (1994, UK #1) and The Fat of the Land (1997, #1 in 26 countries). Licensed Roy Davis Jr.'s Chicago house record 'Gabriel' for the British market in 1997.

name: XXXTentacion
aliases: Jahseh Dwayne Ricardo Onfroy; X; XXX
description: XXXTentacion, born Jahseh Dwayne Ricardo Onfroy on January 23, 1998, in Plantation, Florida, and raised largely in Lauderhill, was a rapper and singer who became a leading figure of the SoundCloud rap and emo-rap movements. He began posting music to SoundCloud in 2013, co-founded the Members Only collective, and broke through with the distorted single "Look at Me!" His debut studio album, 17 (2017), built around depression and isolation, debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200, and its follow-up, ? (March 2018), debuted at No. 1. Onfroy's career was also marked by serious legal trouble, including domestic-abuse charges pending at his death. On June 18, 2018, at age 20, he was shot and killed during a robbery outside a motorcycle dealership in Deerfield Beach, Florida. In the week after his death, "Sad!" rose to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, making him the first artist to top that chart posthumously as a lead artist since the Notorious B.I.G. in 1997, and the posthumous album Skins (2018) became his second No. 1 album.

name: X-Clan
description: X-Clan is the Brooklyn group that fused Parliament-Funkadelic groove to Black nationalist instruction and became the standard-bearer of hip-hop's Afrocentric wave. Its original members carried ritual titles: Brother J, the Grand Verbalizer; Professor X, the Overseer; Paradise, the Architect; and DJ Sugar Shaft, the Rhythm Provider. The group was the best-known component of the Blackwatch Movement, the Brooklyn activist organization Professor X helped build and his father, Sonny "Abubadika" Carson, led. Their debut To the East, Blackwards (1990), released on 4th & B'Way/Island, ran eleven tracks — "Funkin' Lesson," "Heed the Word of the Brother," "A Day of Outrage" — over thick P-Funk samples, with Professor X's recurring benediction that the work was protected by the Red, the Black and the Green. Brother J, who called himself a pitbull for Black nationalism, has carried the X-Clan name forward with later lineups. CultureTechLens profiled X-Clan in Short #177.

name: Xavier Vance
description: Xavier Vance is the executive chef and co-founder of Southern Chicago, the South Loop restaurant he created with Troy Vivrett, aiming — in his words at opening — to reintroduce Chicagoans and visitors to Southern American cuisine with a fine-dining approach to classic Southern dishes. The restaurant's own team listing and trade coverage give his titles as Executive Chef and Co-Founder; the additional 'CEO' title appears on WVON's roster only and is carried as rostered. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.
